name: Sallu
overview: Sallu is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Meshullam. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or detailed narrative provided. His primary distinction lies in his genealogical placement within the Benjaminite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Sallu' is a proper name meaning 'restored.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew term as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:7.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Sallu is the son of Meshullam and a descendant of Benjamin. Beyond this, no further family relationships or connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Sallu's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his genealogical role within the tribe of Benjamin, as preserved in the post-exilic genealogies. His mention underscores the continuity of the Benjaminite line, contributing to the restoration and preservation of Israel's tribal identities after the exile.
